meta.title: My English Book
meta.subtitle: Pupil's Book · Class 1
meta.authors: Written for the Class 1 Integrated Scheme of Work (EFEDI Schools, 2025/2026)
insideCover: Write your name on this page. Draw a sun and colour it yellow.
If you find this book, please return it to the school.
howToUse: Every week is one unit. One unit takes five short lessons of 30 minutes.
Each unit follows the same seven steps, so you learn the routine once: Let's start · Listen and say · Read · Write · New words and grammar · Phonics · Rhyme, song or drama.
In the middle of the unit you find "I integrate" — a small real-life task where you use everything you have learned that week.
At the end of the unit there is a mini project. Step by step, the mini projects build the theme strip you present in week 4 of each theme.
The last box of every unit is "Check yourself". Nobody marks it for you: you decide if you can do it, then colour the star.
Do not write in the book if the school re-uses copies — say the answers aloud or use an exercise book.

cba.title: How this book works — learning by doing
cba.intro: This book follows the Competency-Based Approach (CBA) of the Cameroon primary curriculum and the seven domains of your Class 1 Integrated Scheme of Work. A competence is not only what you know: it is what you can do, in a real situation, with what you know.

blocks.title: 1. We start from a real situation
blocks.text: Every week opens with "Let's start": a small scene from home, the market, the road, the classroom or the playground. You talk about it before you read or write anything. English must be useful from the first minute.

blocks.title: 2. Seven domains, one week
blocks.text: Your scheme gives seven domains: Listening and Speaking, Reading, Writing, Grammar/Vocabulary/Pronunciation, Phonics, Literature and Drama, and the Culminating Project. Each week in this book has one step for each of them, in that order.

blocks.title: 3. I integrate
blocks.text: In the middle of each unit, a task asks you to use the week's words, sounds and sentences together — for example, give directions to a visitor, or ask politely to borrow a broom. This is the heart of the CBA.

blocks.title: 4. The mini project builds the strip
blocks.text: Each week you add one small thing to a strip: a drawing, a label, a sentence, a polite phrase. After four weeks the strip is complete and you present it — My Home Snapshot Strip, My Village/Town Strip, My School Day Strip, What People Do Strip, How We Travel Strip, Staying Clean Strip, My Game Strip, How We Communicate Strip.

blocks.title: 5. You check yourself
blocks.text: Every unit ends with three criteria and three levels: Not yet, Getting there, Yes, I can. Your teacher uses the same criteria. Nobody has to fail: you practise until you can say "Yes, I can".

stripGuide.title: My strip: what I need
stripGuide.intro: A strip is a long piece of paper or card folded into four parts — one part for each week of the theme. Keep it in your folder. You will present it in the last week of the theme.
materials: A strip of paper or card, folded in four
Your exercise book for writing labels
rules: Draw big and clear. Colour inside the lines.
Write the label under the drawing, in English.
One part of the strip = one week. Do not jump ahead.
Keep your spelling neat: copy the words from the book.
Present your strip standing up, looking at your friends, with a loud clear voice.

usefulSentences: May I borrow your pencil, please?
What is this? — It is a ______.
Where is the ______? — It is near the ______.
Où est le ______ ? — Il est près de ______.
What is your name? — My name is ______.

themes.title: The Home
themes.blurb: At home with Mother, Father, Grandmother and the baby. We greet, name objects, use polite words and describe what we do at home.
objectives: Recognize, pronounce, and trace basic letter sounds and common home-related vocabulary
Demonstrate polite expressions and greetings in home settings
Identify tools and objects in the home through words, images, and actions
Decode and spell monosyllabic words connected to routines and spaces
Compose short oral and written phrases introducing people and places at home
Participate in storytelling, singing, and simple role-play about life at home
projectSteps: Create a strip with a drawing of their home and three labeled items
Add a greeting phrase and polite expression
Include a short sentence introducing one family member
Perform a rhyme or song related to life at home

write.task: Trace the curves, the zigzag lines and the letters B, M, S, D.

language.grammarInstruction: Look at the box with your teacher. Then say the examples.
box: We say Hi! Hello! Good morning! to greet somebody.
I am happy. You are kind. — I and you are pronouns.

phonics.instruction: Say the sound. Then find the sound in each word.

In my house, I find my cup,

miniProject.label: Mini project
miniProject.instruction: Add this to your theme strip.

rubric.title: Check yourself
rubric.instruction: Tick how you are doing. Colour a star when you can do it alone.

Participate in songs, stories, rhymes, and dialogue connected to daily community life
projectSteps: Create a strip showing 3 places in their village/town with drawings and labels
Add short phrases describing one person and place

Recite a rhyme or short chant about daily life in the village or town

units.title: Naming and Talking About Games
units.competence: name indoor and outdoor games and the things we play with
units.compSentence: By the end of this week I can name indoor and outdoor games and the things we play with.

situation.label: Let's start
situation.text: Break time. Some pupils play outside, some play inside the classroom because it is raining.
questions: Which games do you play outside?
Which games do you play inside?

listen.title: Naming games
listen.instruction: Listen to your teacher. Then say each line with your teacher.

read.title: Reading game names
read.instruction: Read with your teacher. Point to each word with your finger.
read.task: Read the word. Then show how you play with it.

write.title: Writing
write.instruction: Write in your exercise book. Sit well and hold your pencil well.
write.task: Write: "ball", "rope", "skip". Then write one sentence: "I like ____."

language.grammarFocus: Common nouns; present tense verbs
language.grammarInstruction: Look at the box with your teacher. Then say the examples.
box: Nouns name the game and the tool: ball, rope, chalk, swing.
Verbs tell the action: throw, jump, skip, play.

phonics.instruction: Say the sound. Then find the sound in each word.

literature.title: Throw and Catch
literature.instruction: Say the rhyme with your teacher. Clap the beat.

integrate.label: I integrate — I use my English
integrate.instruction: Work with a friend. Use all the English you have learned this week.
integrate.task: Tell your friend your favourite game and its tool: "I like skipping. I use a rope."

miniProject.label: Mini project
miniProject.instruction: Add this to your theme strip.
miniProject.text: Draw and label one game and its tool.

rubric.title: Check yourself
rubric.instruction: Tick how you are doing. Colour a star when you can do it alone.
criteria: I can name five games and their tools.
I can say what I do with a ball and a rope.
I can label a drawing of a game.

units.title: Playing Together and Giving Instructions
units.competence: give and follow simple instructions when we play
units.compSentence: By the end of this week I can give and follow simple instructions when we play.

situation.label: Let's start
situation.text: You are the captain of your team. Your friends do not know the game. You must explain it.
questions: What do you say first?
How do you explain the next action?

listen.title: Giving and following instructions
listen.instruction: Listen to your teacher. Then say each line with your teacher.

read.title: Reading action sentences
read.instruction: Read with your teacher. Point to each word with your finger.
read.task: Read the instruction. Then do it.

write.title: Writing
write.instruction: Write in your exercise book. Sit well and hold your pencil well.
write.task: Write two instructions for a game. Use and or then.

language.grammarFocus: Imperative verbs; conjunctions and, then
language.grammarInstruction: Look at the box with your teacher. Then say the examples.
box: An instruction starts with a verb: Throw the ball. Jump now.
We use then for the next action: Sit, then stand.

phonics.focus: Final sounds in game and action words
phonics.instruction: Say the sound. Then find the sound in each word.

literature.title: Play With Me
literature.instruction: Say the rhyme with your teacher. Clap the beat.

integrate.label: I integrate — I use my English
integrate.instruction: Work with a friend. Use all the English you have learned this week.
integrate.task: Be the captain. Give three instructions. Your team follows them correctly.

miniProject.label: Mini project
miniProject.instruction: Add this to your theme strip.
miniProject.text: Add one instruction or game-related request to the strip.

rubric.title: Check yourself
rubric.instruction: Tick how you are doing. Colour a star when you can do it alone.
criteria: I can give three clear play instructions.
I can use and and then.
I can follow my friend's instructions.

units.title: Playing Safely and Using Polite Words
units.competence: use polite words and rules so that everybody plays safely
units.compSentence: By the end of this week I can use polite words and rules so that everybody plays safely.

situation.label: Let's start
situation.text: Two pupils are playing with the only rope. You also want to play, but you must ask politely.
questions: What do you say to them?
What rules keep the game safe?

listen.title: Saying polite words at play
listen.instruction: Listen to your teacher. Then say each line with your teacher.

read.title: Reading play rules
read.instruction: Read with your teacher. Point to each word with your finger.
read.task: Read each rule. Then say if it is polite or not.

write.title: Writing
write.instruction: Write in your exercise book. Sit well and hold your pencil well.
write.task: Write two polite sentences for the playground.

language.grammarFocus: Modal verbs (Can, May); sentence punctuation
language.grammarInstruction: Look at the box with your teacher. Then say the examples.
box: Can I join? May I use the chalk?
Polite questions end with a question mark.

phonics.focus: Digraphs in polite and play words
phonics.instruction: Say the sound. Then find the sound in each word.

literature.title: Playing Together Politely
lines: Bih: Can I join your game?
Ngo: Yes, you can. Wait your turn.
Bih: May I use the rope first?
literature.instruction: Act it out in pairs. Speak loudly and politely.

integrate.label: I integrate — I use my English
integrate.instruction: Work with a friend. Use all the English you have learned this week.
integrate.task: Act the dialogue. Then make one rule for your class playground and say it politely.

miniProject.label: Mini project
miniProject.instruction: Add this to your theme strip.
miniProject.text: Add a polite request or a rule to the strip.

rubric.title: Check yourself
rubric.instruction: Tick how you are doing. Colour a star when you can do it alone.
criteria: I can ask to join a game politely.
I can say three rules for safe play.
I can read and spell chalk, shout, chair.

units.title: Describing Favorite Games and Final Presentation
units.competence: describe my favourite game and present my work
units.compSentence: By the end of this week I can describe my favourite game and present my work.

situation.label: Let's start
situation.text: Your teacher asks: "What is your favourite game, and why?"
questions: What is your favourite game?
Who do you play it with?

listen.title: Talking about favourite games
listen.instruction: Listen to your teacher. Then say each line with your teacher.

read.title: Reviewing play sentences
read.instruction: Read with your teacher. Point to each word with your finger.
read.task: Read the sentences. Then say which game you like.

write.title: Writing
write.instruction: Write in your exercise book. Sit well and hold your pencil well.
write.task: Write three sentences about your favourite game. Correct "she like jump" first.

language.grammarFocus: Sentence editing; adjectives and capitalisation
language.grammarInstruction: Look at the box with your teacher. Then say the examples.
box: she like jump → She likes to jump. he play game → He plays a fun game.
Add -s with he, she, it.

phonics.instruction: Clap the syllables. Then write the word.

literature.title: My Game Strip
lines: This is my game. (show the strip)
I jump the rope with my friend. (jump)
We play fair and we are polite. (smile)
literature.instruction: Present your strip to the class. Speak clearly and smile.

integrate.label: I integrate — I use my English
integrate.instruction: Work with a friend. Use all the English you have learned this week.
integrate.task: Present your strip and teach the class one game in English, using instructions.

miniProject.label: Mini project
miniProject.instruction: Add this to your theme strip.
miniProject.text: Finalise the strip with drawings, instructions and a chant.

rubric.title: Check yourself
rubric.instruction: Tick how you are doing. Colour a star when you can do it alone.
criteria: I can describe my favourite game.
I can correct a sentence with the verb -s.
I can present my My Game Strip and teach a game.

themes.title: Communication
themes.blurb: How we send and receive messages: talking, a letter, the radio, the phone. We say how we feel, ask politely and share a message.
objectives: Identify common communication methods and tools (verbal, non-verbal, digital, and traditional)
Use appropriate greetings, expressions, and descriptive vocabulary during communication
Read, write, and decode basic words related to expressing ideas, messages, and feelings
Apply grammar structures including sentence types, pronouns, and punctuation for clarity
Engage in dialogue, chant, storytelling, and role-play about exchanging messages and feelings
projectSteps: Create a strip showing two forms of communication (e.g., talking and messaging) with drawings and labels
Add greeting and expression phrases for sharing ideas politely
Include one chant or short role-play about giving and receiving a message
Present the strip with clear explanation and oral performance

units.title: Naming Communication Forms and Tools
units.competence: name the ways and tools we use to send messages
units.compSentence: By the end of this week I can name the ways and tools we use to send messages.

situation.label: Let's start
situation.text: Your father is in Douala. You want to tell him about your school prize.
questions: How can you send him a message?
What do you say to him?

listen.title: Naming communication tools
listen.instruction: Listen to your teacher. Then say each line with your teacher.

read.title: Reading communication words
read.instruction: Read with your teacher. Point to each word with your finger.
read.task: Read the word. Then say how you use it.

write.title: Writing
write.instruction: Write in your exercise book. Sit well and hold your pencil well.
write.task: Write: "She calls." "He writes." Then label your drawing.

language.grammarFocus: Common nouns; personal pronouns
language.grammarInstruction: Look at the box with your teacher. Then say the examples.
box: Nouns name the tools: phone, letter, radio, drum.
Pronouns replace names: She calls. He writes. I talk.

phonics.instruction: Say the sound. Then find the sound in each word.

literature.title: Say It Right
literature.instruction: Say the rhyme with your teacher. Clap the beat.

integrate.label: I integrate — I use my English
integrate.instruction: Work with a friend. Use all the English you have learned this week.
integrate.task: Show three ways to send a message without words: a wave, a smile, a drum. Say what each one means.

miniProject.label: Mini project
miniProject.instruction: Add this to your theme strip.
miniProject.text: Draw and label one form of communication (phone, letter or speech).

rubric.title: Check yourself
rubric.instruction: Tick how you are doing. Colour a star when you can do it alone.
criteria: I can name four communication tools.
I can say how I send a message.
I can label a drawing of a communication tool.

units.title: Expressing Feelings and Ideas
units.competence: say how I feel and how other people feel
units.compSentence: By the end of this week I can say how I feel and how other people feel.

situation.label: Let's start
situation.text: Your friend lost her pen. She is looking at the ground and she is quiet.
questions: How does she feel?
What do you say to her?

listen.title: Saying how we feel
listen.instruction: Listen to your teacher. Then say each line with your teacher.

read.title: Reading feeling words
read.instruction: Read with your teacher. Point to each word with your finger.
read.task: Read the sentence. Then show the feeling on your face.

write.title: Writing
write.instruction: Write in your exercise book. Sit well and hold your pencil well.
write.task: Write two sentences: "I am ____ today." "My friend is ____."

language.grammarFocus: Interjections and adjectives
language.grammarInstruction: Look at the box with your teacher. Then say the examples.
box: Interjections show feeling: Oh! Wow! Sorry!
Adjectives tell how somebody is: happy, sad, kind, calm.

phonics.instruction: Say the sound. Then find the sound in each word.

literature.title: How I Feel
literature.instruction: Say the rhyme with your teacher. Clap the beat.

integrate.label: I integrate — I use my English
integrate.instruction: Work with a friend. Use all the English you have learned this week.
integrate.task: Make a feelings face. Your friend looks at it and says: "You are happy!" or "You are sad."

miniProject.label: Mini project
miniProject.instruction: Add this to your theme strip.
miniProject.text: Add one feeling or expression phrase to the strip.

rubric.title: Check yourself
rubric.instruction: Tick how you are doing. Colour a star when you can do it alone.
criteria: I can say how I feel.
I can describe how a friend feels.
I can use Wow!, Oh! and Sorry! correctly.

units.title: Asking and Answering Questions Politely
units.competence: ask and answer questions clearly and politely
units.compSentence: By the end of this week I can ask and answer questions clearly and politely.

situation.label: Let's start
situation.text: A new pupil comes into your class. She does not know anybody.
questions: What do you ask her?
How do you answer her questions?

listen.title: Asking polite questions
listen.instruction: Listen to your teacher. Then say each line with your teacher.

read.title: Reading questions and answers
read.instruction: Read with your teacher. Point to each word with your finger.
items: Who are you? I am Sam.
What is this? It is a book.
Where is the teacher? He is in the class.
read.task: Read the question, then read the answer.

write.title: Writing
write.instruction: Write in your exercise book. Sit well and hold your pencil well.
write.task: Write two questions and two answers. Remember the question mark.

language.grammarFocus: Question words who, what, where; punctuation
language.grammarInstruction: Look at the box with your teacher. Then say the examples.
box: We ask with Who…? What…? Where…?
Every question ends with a question mark (?).

phonics.focus: Digraphs in question and answer words
phonics.instruction: Say the sound. Then find the sound in each word.

literature.title: Asking and Answering
lines: Ngo: My name is Ngo. Who are you?
Bih: I am Bih. Where do you live?
Ngo: I live near the school.
literature.instruction: Act it out in pairs. Speak loudly and politely.

integrate.label: I integrate — I use my English
integrate.instruction: Work with a friend. Use all the English you have learned this week.
integrate.task: Interview a friend with three questions. Then tell the class about your friend.

miniProject.label: Mini project
miniProject.instruction: Add this to your theme strip.
miniProject.text: Add a question or an answer sentence to the strip.

rubric.title: Check yourself
rubric.instruction: Tick how you are doing. Colour a star when you can do it alone.
criteria: I can ask questions with who, what, where.
I can answer questions in a full sentence.
I can read and spell what, she, where.

units.title: Sharing Messages and Final Presentation
units.competence: give a simple message clearly and present my communication strip
units.compSentence: By the end of this week I can give a simple message clearly and present my communication strip.

situation.label: Let's start
situation.text: You must take a message to your neighbour: his son is coming home today.
questions: What is your message?
How do you say it politely?

listen.title: Sharing a message
listen.instruction: Listen to your teacher. Then say each line with your teacher.

read.title: Reading message sentences
read.instruction: Read with your teacher. Point to each word with your finger.
read.task: Read the message. Then say who it is for.

write.title: Writing
write.instruction: Write in your exercise book. Sit well and hold your pencil well.
write.task: Write a short message to a friend. Correct "they write letter" first.

language.grammarFocus: Editing messages; review of sentence types and punctuation
language.grammarInstruction: Look at the box with your teacher. Then say the examples.
box: she call him → She called him. they write letter → They write a letter.
Check: capital letter, verb, full stop or question mark.

phonics.instruction: Clap the syllables. Then write the word.

literature.title: How We Communicate Strip
lines: This is a phone. I call my father. (show the strip)
This is a letter. I write a message. (write motion)
Talk with care and be polite. (smile)
literature.instruction: Present your strip to the class. Speak clearly and smile.

integrate.label: I integrate — I use my English
integrate.instruction: Work with a friend. Use all the English you have learned this week.
integrate.task: Present your strip to the class. Give your message clearly, then answer two questions.

miniProject.label: Mini project
miniProject.instruction: Add this to your theme strip.
miniProject.text: Finalise and present the communication strip with tools, phrases and a chant.

rubric.title: Check yourself
rubric.instruction: Tick how you are doing. Colour a star when you can do it alone.
criteria: I can give a message clearly.
I can correct a message sentence.
I can present my How We Communicate Strip.
